subject: Polity
q: Which Article of the Constitution of India safeguards one's right to marry the person of one's choice?
exp: In the Hadiya case (2018), the Supreme Court held that the right to marry a person of one's choice is an integral part of Article 21.

subject: Polity
q: A Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha can be delayed by the Rajya Sabha for a maximum period of:
exp: Under Article 109, the Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill within 14 days, failing which it is deemed passed by both Houses.

subject: Polity
q: Under the Indian Constitution, concentration of wealth violates:
options: The Directive Principles of State Policy
exp: Article 39(c) under DPSP directs the State to ensure that the economic system does not result in the concentration of wealth to the common detriment.

subject: Polity
q: Which Schedule of the Constitution of India contains special provisions for the administration and control of Scheduled Areas in states other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram?
exp: The Fifth Schedule deals with Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in states other than the four northeastern states (which are covered under the Sixth Schedule).

subject: Polity
q: Who decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not?
exp: Under Article 110(3), the decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha on whether a Bill is a Money Bill is final.

subject: Polity
q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act lowered the voting age from 21 years to 18 years?
exp: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 amended Article 326 to lower the voting age for Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections from 21 to 18.

subject: Polity
q: The power to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights is vested in:
options: Both Supreme Court and High Courts
exp: Under Article 32 (Supreme Court) and Article 226 (High Courts), both can issue writs such as Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto.

subject: Polity
q: Which of the following is NOT a Constitutional Body?
exp: NITI Aayog is an extra-constitutional (non-statutory) executive body created by a Cabinet resolution in 2015.

subject: Polity
q: The Anti-Defection Law is contained in which Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
exp: The Tenth Schedule was inserted by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985 to curb political defections.

subject: Polity
q: In the Parliament of India, the 'Zero Hour' refers to:
options: The first hour of every parliamentary sitting
An informal device to raise matters without prior notice
The time reserved exclusively for Money Bills
The last hour before adjournment sine die
exp: Zero Hour is an Indian parliamentary innovation starting immediately after Question Hour, allowing MPs to raise urgent matters without prior notice.

subject: Polity
q: Which of the following writs literally means 'by what authority or warrant'?
exp: Quo Warranto is issued by a court to enquire into the legality of a claim of a person to a public office.

subject: Polity
q: The 'Basic Structure' doctrine of the Indian Constitution was propounded by the Supreme Court in:
exp: In Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973), a 13-judge bench ruled that Parliament cannot alter the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution under Article 368.

subject: Polity
q: The Council of Ministers in the Union Government is collectively responsible to:
exp: Under Article 75(3), the Union Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the House of the People (Lok Sabha).

subject: Polity
q: Which Article empowers the President of India to promulgate Ordinances during the recess of Parliament?
exp: Article 123 grants ordinance-making power to the President (while Article 213 grants similar power to the Governor of a State).

subject: Polity
q: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 is related to:
exp: The 73rd Amendment added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution, giving constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions.

subject: Polity
q: Who presides over a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament?
exp: Under Article 118(4), the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting (summoned by the President under Article 108).

subject: Polity
q: The Finance Commission of India is constituted by the President every five years under:
exp: Article 280 provides for a quasi-judicial Finance Commission to recommend the distribution of tax revenues between the Centre and the States.

subject: Polity
q: Which Fundamental Right is available ONLY to citizens of India and NOT to foreigners?
options: Article 21 (Protection of life and personal liberty)
exp: Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30 are available exclusively to Indian citizens; Articles 14, 20, 21, 21A, 22, 23, 24, 25–28 apply to foreigners as well.
